summary: Build the frontend acceptance checklist for the Angular acceptance harness. Composes a typed API client for acceptance-suite endpoints, a React/Next.js AcceptanceChecklist component that renders each acceptance scenario linked to live API data, a useAcceptanceChecklist hook for polling-based state management with all required UI states (loading, empty, running, success, blocked, stale, backend-failure, reconnect), and a dedicated page route to serve the checklist. No G01–G09 production UX is duplicated; the checklist reads exclusively from backend snapshots and events. Phase A boundary: no full G01–G09 workflow UX, no Jira completion claim.

implementation_steps.description: This plan document — read-only planner output

Add TypeScript types for all acceptance-suite DTOs consumed by the frontend. Add these types after the existing ArtifactRefDto type (around line 34): (A) HarnessFixtureType — union literal type with 7 string values matching the Python enum ('angular_180x', 'angular_182x', 'passable', 'compiler_error', 'dependency_conflict', 'environment_blocker', 'cancellable'); (B) HarnessRequestDto — fixture_type (HarnessFixtureType), name (string), idempotency_key (string|null), expected_state_version (number), actor (string); (C) HarnessResultDto — fixture_id (string), fixture_root (string), outcome (string), evidence_refs (ArtifactRefDto[]), state_version (number), idempotent_replay (boolean); (D) HarnessEvaluateRequestDto — fixture_id (string); (E) HarnessStatusDto — overall_status (string), fixtures (HarnessResultDto[]), errors (string[]), evidence_summary (Record<string, string | number | string[]>); (F) HarnessRunStatusDto — run_id (string), suite_id (string), overall_status (string), fixture_count (number), passed (number), failed (number), started_at (string|null), completed_at (string|null), evidence_refs (ArtifactRefDto[]). All types follow the existing pattern: exported type aliases, optional fields marked with ? where appropriate. Do not remove or modify existing types.

Create the acceptance-suite API client module following the pattern in runs.ts. Export typed functions: (1) getAcceptanceStatus(client?) -> Promise<HarnessStatusDto> — calls GET /api/v1/operator/acceptance-suite/status; (2) createAcceptanceFixture(request: HarnessRequestDto, client?) -> Promise<HarnessResultDto> — calls POST /api/v1/operator/acceptance-suite/fixtures; (3) evaluateAcceptanceFixture(request: HarnessEvaluateRequestDto, client?) -> Promise<HarnessResultDto> — calls POST /api/v1/operator/acceptance-suite/fixtures/evaluate; (4) listHarnessRuns(client?) -> Promise<Array<{run_id: string, artifact_count: number, latest_event: string|null}>> — calls GET /api/v1/operator/acceptance-suite/runs; (5) getHarnessRun(runId: string, client?) -> Promise<HarnessRunStatusDto> — calls GET /api/v1/operator/acceptance-suite/runs/{encodeURIComponent(runId)}; (6) getHarnessRunEvidence(runId: string, client?) -> Promise<ArtifactRefDto[]> — calls GET /api/v1/operator/acceptance-suite/runs/{encodeURIComponent(runId)}/evidence. Each function accepts optional client parameter defaulting to the shared apiClient singleton. Use encodeURIComponent for path segments. Import types from @/types/generated/api.

Create a polling-based hook that manages acceptance-suite state. Export type ChecklistConnectionStatus = 'loading' | 'idle' | 'polling' | 'stale' | 'backend-failure' | 'reconnect-required'. Export interface UseAcceptanceChecklistResult { status: ChecklistConnectionStatus; suiteStatus: HarnessStatusDto | null; runDetails: HarnessRunStatusDto | null; error: string | null; start: (fixtureType: HarnessFixtureType, name?: string) => Promise<HarnessResultDto>; evaluate: (fixtureId: string) => Promise<HarnessResultDto>; refresh: () => Promise<void>; evidence: ArtifactRefDto[];}. Implementation: (1) useState for status, suiteStatus, runDetails, error, evidence; (2) useRef for polling interval, abort controller; (3) refresh() function calls getAcceptanceStatus() — sets status='polling' on success, 'backend-failure' on network error; (4) start() calls createAcceptanceFixture then immediately calls refresh(); (5) evaluate() calls evaluateAcceptanceFixture then refresh(); (6) useEffect with setInterval(5000) calling refresh() when status is 'polling' or 'idle'; (7) On consecutive failures (>3), set status='reconnect-required'; (8) On stale state_version detection from backend response, set status='stale'; (9) cleanup: clearInterval and abort in effect return. All state reads from backend snapshots only — no local workflow advancement. Imports from @/api/acceptance and @/types/generated/api.

Create CSS Module following the ControlTowerShell.module.css pattern. Include classes: .shell (max-width 1220px, margin 0 auto, padding 2rem), .header (flexbox with gap), .connectionBar (inline-flex pill, green for idle, blue for polling, red for backend-failure, amber for stale), .scenarioGrid (card grid with 3 columns on desktop, 1 on mobile), .scenarioCard (panel-style card with border, background, padding, rounding), .scenarioPass (green accent border), .scenarioFail (red accent border), .scenarioPending (neutral border), .scenarioBlocked (amber accent border), .scenarioTitle (bold, color var), .scenarioStatus (inline badge with appropriate colors), .scenarioMeta (grid of dt/dd pairs for fixture type, outcome, version), .evidenceList (stacked list with border separators), .evidenceItem (flex row, code for path, span for checksum), .actionBar (flex row for Start/Evaluate buttons), .button (styled per existing design: background, border, rounding, font-weight), .button:disabled (opacity reduce, cursor not-allowed), .errorBanner (red background border), .emptyState (centered note), .twoColumns (grid 2 cols), .pipeline (horizontal step indicator for scenario progression). All on dark theme (#09111f background, #eef4ff text, #5a8cff primary accent). Responsive breakpoints for <900px (single column) and <680px (compact padding).

Create the operator acceptance checklist React component. 'use client' directive. Props: initialStatus (HarnessStatusDto | null), runId (string | null). Implementation: (1) Use useAcceptanceChecklist hook for state management; (2) Render a connection bar showing the current ChecklistConnectionStatus with appropriate visual styling (green='All systems nominal', blue='Checking backend…', red='Backend unreachable — retrying', amber='State is stale — refresh', yellow='Reconnection needed'); (3) Render a header with title 'Operator Acceptance Checklist', subtitle 'Angular Acceptance Harness — Phase A', and a dimension grid showing overall_status, fixture count, error count, evidence summary; (4) Render a scenario grid where each HarnessFixtureType is a scenario card linking to the corresponding live data: for each fixture type in the fixtures list, render a scenario card showing fixture_type label, outcome badge (SUCCEEDED=green, FAILED=red, PENDING=grey, BLOCKED=amber), fixture_id, fixture_root path, state_version, evidence_refs linked to artifact preview links; (5) For fixture types not yet in the fixtures list, render a pending card with 'Not yet evaluated' status and a 'Start' button; (6) Action bar: buttons for triggering fixture generation and evaluation, disabled when status is not 'idle' or 'polling'; (7) Evidence panel: for each selected fixture, render its ArtifactRefDto list with artifact_type badge, relative_path, checksum — each linked to the existing artifact preview infrastructure (reuse ArtifactPreviewPanel with initial artifact metadata); (8) Error banner: when error is non-null, render a styled error section with the error message; (9) Run details section: when runId is provided and runDetails is available, render HarnessRunStatusDto fields (run_id, suite_id, overall_status, fixture_count, passed/failed counts, started_at/completed_at timestamps); (10) Empty state: when suiteStatus is not null and fixtures.length === 0, render 'No fixtures have been evaluated. Create a fixture to begin.' with a prominent action button; (11) Links each acceptance scenario to live product artifacts by embedding ArtifactRefDto evidence_refs in each scenario card with artifact_id hrefs pointing to the existing artifact fetch mechanism. No G01–G09 production UX is duplicated. No hidden API-only completion tracking.

Create the acceptance checklist page route under Next.js App Router. Export dynamic = 'force-dynamic' to ensure fresh data on every request. Default async export function AcceptancePage(): (1) On the server, call the acceptance API client directly to fetch initial status (getAcceptanceStatus) — this SSR's the initial state so the page renders immediately; (2) On fetch failure, catch the error and return a minimal fallback <main> with error message and a 'Retry' link; (3) Render the client-side AcceptanceChecklist component passing the server-fetched initialStatus and an optional runId (initially null, the user selects a run client-side); (4) Page layout: full-width shell within the existing globals.css theme. Import AcceptanceChecklist from @/components/AcceptanceChecklist. Import getAcceptanceStatus from @/api/acceptance.

Create vitest tests for the acceptance API module. Test groups: (A) Request construction — each function sends correct HTTP method and path; (B) Response parsing — valid JSON responses are parsed to the correct TypeScript types; (C) Error handling — backend 4xx/5xx responses throw ApiClientError with correct status, path, and message; (D) Client injection — passing a custom fetch implementation works (mock fetch returning canned responses); (E) Edge cases — empty response arrays, null values in DTOs, special characters in run_id are properly encoded. Use vi.fn() for mock fetch, vi.mock() for client.ts imports. Pattern follows existing __tests__ files in frontend/src/api/__tests__/.

Create vitest tests for the useAcceptanceChecklist hook. Test groups: (A) Initial state — status is 'loading', suiteStatus is null, error is null; (B) Successful startup — after initial refresh, status transitions to 'polling', suiteStatus is populated; (C) Backend failure — consecutive API failures set status to 'backend-failure' (after 3 retries) and then 'reconnect-required' (after 6 retries); (D) Start fixture — calling start() sends POST to /fixtures and triggers a refresh of status; (E) Evaluate fixture — calling evaluate() sends POST to /fixtures/evaluate and triggers refresh; (F) Stale state detection — when state_version in response differs from previous version, status becomes 'stale'; (G) Cleanup — unmounting the component clears the polling interval and aborts pending requests; (H) Edge cases — empty fixture list, null runDetails, network timeout. Use renderHook from @testing-library/react with a wrapper pattern. Mock the acceptance API module with vi.mock().

Create vitest tests for the AcceptanceChecklist component. Test groups using @testing-library/react render + screen assertions: (A) Loading state — renders a 'Connecting to backend…' connection bar and no scenario grid; (B) Empty state — suiteStatus with fixtures=[] renders 'No fixtures have been evaluated' message and an action button; (C) Running state — suiteStatus with evaluation-in-progress renders scenario cards with PENDING badges and spinner indicators; (D) Success state — completed fixture with outcome='SUCCEEDED' renders green PASS badge with evidence_refs as clickable artifact links; (E) Blocked state — fixture with outcome='BLOCKED' renders amber blocked badge with error message; (F) Backend-failure state — status='backend-failure' renders red connection bar and retry prompt; (G) Stale state — status='stale' renders amber connection bar with 'State is stale — refresh' message; (H) All scenario cards render fixture_type label correctly; (I) Evidence refs render artifact_type badge, relative_path, and checksum; (J) Action buttons are disabled when status is not 'idle' or 'polling'; (K) Error banner renders when error prop is non-null; (L) Accessibility: connection bar has role='status' aria-live='polite', buttons have accessible names, scenario cards have aria-labels; (M) Snapshot test for the full state with all 7 fixture types in various outcomes. vi.mock('@/hooks/useAcceptanceChecklist') returning canned state for each test scenario. Pattern follows AuthoritativeRunDashboard.test.tsx.

risks.description: Backend DTO shape changes — if T01/T02 are still evolving, the frontend types and API client may need synchronization after backend settles
risks.mitigation: Frontend types in generated/api.ts are manually synchronized. Pin to the exact backend contract shapes documented above. If backend changes, update types as a coordinated step before merging T03.

risks.description: Polling vs SSE — the acceptance checklist uses polling (setInterval 5s) instead of SSE events, which could produce slightly stale data compared to the event-driven production UX
risks.mitigation: Polling is intentional for Phase A: acceptance-suite events are optional per S4-F15. The checklist is read-only monitoring. If SSE becomes available in Phase B, the hook can switch to EventSource while keeping the same component interface.

risks.description: No WebSocket/SSE for harness events — useAcceptanceChecklist cannot detect mid-evaluation state changes in real time, only the last snapshot
risks.mitigation: 5-second polling is adequate for operator monitoring. The hook exposes status='polling' while waiting and status='stale' when data doesn't advance. Phase B can add SSE event subscription for the acceptance-suite optional events.

risks.description: Artifact preview integration — evidence links in the checklist need to interoperate with existing ArtifactPreviewPanel which expects artifact content to be loadable via artifact_id
risks.mitigation: The checklist passes ArtifactRefDto items to ArtifactPreviewPanel. Ensure the artifact content endpoint (GET /artifacts/{artifact_id}) works for harness-prefixed artifact_ids. If not, the checklist shows metadata without preview until Phase B.

risks.description: CSS Module class name conflict — AcceptanceChecklist.module.css may duplicate class names from ControlTowerShell.module.css
risks.mitigation: CSS Modules scope class names locally. Import shared classes from ControlTowerShell.module.css where appropriate (e.g., styles.panel, styles.shell, styles.connectionBar). New classes use distinctive names (scenarioCard, scenarioGrid, etc.) to avoid ambiguity.

risks.description: Manual type synchronization drift — generated/api.ts is manually updated and may drift from the Python backend contracts
risks.mitigation: Add a brief comment header noting that acceptance-suite types were synchronized as of Phase A. In Phase B, consider auto-generating TypeScript types from the OpenAPI schema.

risks.description: No frontend creation/admin of harness runs — the operator can only view status; run lifecycle management (create, cancel, restart) is backend-initiated only
risks.mitigation: Phase B may expose full lifecycle controls. Phase A is read-only monitoring per the acceptance checklist spec. Document that run creation/deletion is out-of-scope for T03.
